# AidenHQ

> AidenHQ is an open-source AI chief of staff and agent team that runs on your own server: your work life, on autopilot. It cuts the noise so you can focus on what matters. Aiden, the chief of staff, reads your Slack, the email you hand it and your meeting notes, turns what needs you into one action item each, follows up with people until each is done, and sends a morning brief. For anything else, describe an agent in a sentence and Aiden designs it, grants it tools, tries it on real work and adds it to the team; agents also build internal apps and keep them running. Agents work as one team: Aiden routes requests, specialists hand off and review each other, and every correction becomes a rule. Every action that changes something is checked in code (it runs by itself, a second AI checks it, or you decide), spend is capped per agent, task and day, and every agent, instruction and app lives in your own git repository. Self-hosted on one Linux server (or a Mac), any model, open source.

## Install

The usual way is one prompt: the user pastes this line into their AI coding assistant (Claude Code, Codex or another),
which then does the whole install and relays its progress:

```text
Set up AidenHQ on my server by following https://aidenhq.ai/prompt.md
```

AI agents installing AidenHQ for a user: read and follow `https://aidenhq.ai/prompt.md`. It covers the two things to ask
the user (where to install, and their email), how to handle secrets, the exact commands, how to relay progress, how to
read the result and how to verify it. The installer runs on the server, never on the user's laptop (unless the user
chose their Mac), and ends with a one-time setup link the user opens in a browser: they create a password and
authenticator, add their OpenRouter key, take three quick steps (recovery key, Telegram, Slack) and start talking to
Aiden. https://aidenhq.ai/start/ shows this flow for people.

Without an AI assistant, run the installer on the server itself:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://get.aidenhq.ai | sh
```

Requirements: Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04 or Debian 12/13 with systemd, 2+ cores, 6+ GB RAM, 60+ GB free disk (4 cores,
8 GB and 100 GB recommended), SSH with a key as root or a user with passwordless sudo; or a Mac with macOS 13+, 12 GB
memory and 60 GB free (it runs in a Lima VM). An OpenRouter key for the models. AidenHQ is free and open source: the
user pays for their own server and their model usage.

## Docs

- [Full site as markdown](https://aidenhq.ai/llms-full.txt): every page below plus the agent install guide, in one file
- [Agent install guide](https://aidenhq.ai/prompt.md): step-by-step instructions for coding agents to install and set up AidenHQ for their user
- [About AidenHQ](https://aidenhq.ai/index.md): the homepage: what AidenHQ is, a day in the workspace, approvals, tools, what you own, and common questions (what it is, how to install, what you need, what it costs, where data lives, licence)
- [Workspace](https://aidenhq.ai/workspace/index.md): shared docs and whiteboards agents co-edit, Slack channels for agents, chat and Aiden, briefs and digests, the board, teammates
- [Agents and teams](https://aidenhq.ai/agents/index.md): agents that run work end to end, the roster, schedules and events, building a new agent from a description, the company handbook, corrections that stick
- [Apps](https://aidenhq.ai/apps/index.md): internal apps built from one sentence, shared behind your company login, and maintained automatically
- [Safety](https://aidenhq.ai/safety/index.md): approval levels, deterministic guardrails, sovereign by design, model choice with zero data retention, budgets
- [Integrations](https://aidenhq.ai/integrations/index.md): Slack, Telegram, Google, GitHub, Jira, Glean, Grafana, ClickHouse, OpenRouter; connect once, grant per agent and per tool
- [Modules and distros](https://aidenhq.ai/modules/index.md): the kernel, the module list, one-step module add, distros, the open marketplace and licences
- [Get started](https://aidenhq.ai/start/index.md): install with your AI assistant in one line, open the link, three quick steps, then talk to Aiden
- [Install guide](https://aidenhq.ai/install/index.md): three ways to install, requirements, what happens next, cost and licence
- [Installer script](https://get.aidenhq.ai): the POSIX shell installer itself, served as plain text (`--help` lists its options)

## Optional

- [Install reference](https://github.com/Aiden-HQ/aidenhq-distro/blob/main/INSTALL.md): installer options, sizing rules and trust model
- [Product documentation](https://github.com/Aiden-HQ/AidenHQ/tree/main/docs): concepts, architecture, configuration and operations
- [Releases](https://github.com/Aiden-HQ/aidenhq-distro/tree/main/releases): release manifests pinning a kernel and each module
